A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DT-CORL for learning from delay-free offline data and deployment under observation delays. Despite the changed title and expanded scope, matching methods, equations, proofs and experiments establish continuity. The main text, figures, tables and appendices are readable.

before.justification: V1 reports original D4RL HalfCheetah, Hopper and Walker2d experiments under deterministic and stochastic delays in Tables 1–2.

after.justification: V2 retains the original experiments and reports additional AntMaze, dexterous manipulation, belief-model ablation and robustness results in Section 5 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The transformer belief model, policy-iteration objectives and deployment procedure are retained. However, v2 removes v1's n-step/Retrace description and 'Multi Steps = 3' hyperparameter without stating whether those updates were discontinued. Its stronger joint-training language also lacks an explicit revised update rule, leaving actual procedural changes unresolved.

E1.justification: V2 expands beyond the three locomotion environments to four goal-conditioned AntMaze tasks and Adroit Pen, Door and Hammer manipulation tasks. It also adds 32- and 64-step delays and Gaussian, exponential and binomial delay scenarios beyond the original fixed and uniform 4/8/16-step settings.

E2.justification: The original Augmented-BC, Augmented-CQL and Belief-CQL comparisons are retained. V2 adds Belief-IQL across locomotion and unadapted IQL/CQL for Hopper in Table 2, plus Augmented-COMBO and DBPT-SAC for AntMaze in Table 1. Ensemble MLP and diffusion belief predictors are also evaluated against the transformer in Figure 2 and Table 3.

E3.justification: The original locomotion return metric and delay protocols remain. New evaluation designs compare predictors under a common 100-epoch budget using prediction MSE and inference latency, vary data availability from 25% to 100% at fixed HalfCheetah delay 8, and sweep transformer depth and width with convergence and memory measurements. These introduce substantial controlled evaluation settings.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's delay sweeps, v2 adds architecture and transformer-capacity ablations, joint versus separately pretrained belief comparisons, and data-availability experiments. It also adds longer-delay and alternative-distribution robustness tests and qualitative 16-step prediction rollouts. Section 5.3 and Appendix C therefore directly examine design choices and failure conditions previously untested.

E5.justification: V1 provides benchmark point estimates without seed counts or standard deviations. V2 Tables 7–8 report the retained locomotion results as mean ± standard deviation over three seeds; Tables 1 and 9 also specify three-seed averages, and new plots report uncertainty. This establishes substantially expanded reporting, not an explicit increase in runs.

E6.justification: All 288 numerical entries from v1 Tables 1–2 are retained as means in v2 Tables 7–8. V2 adds substantial task, baseline, ablation and robustness results. For example, Table 11 newly reports 105.20 for DT-CORL versus 0.22 for Belief-CQL on Hammer-expert-v1 with deterministic delay 16, while Table 1 exposes near-zero performance on large-play AntMaze.

T1.justification: The Lipschitz definitions, delayed-MDP formulation, Lemmas 4.1–4.2, Proposition 4.3 and associated derivations and proof are substantively retained. V1 Appendix A becomes v2 Appendix B. Changes to indices, notation, wording and cross-references do not introduce new theoretical results or revise the mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contribution—learning delay-robust policies solely from delay-free offline data through belief-constrained policy iteration—remains. V2 broadens the abstract's comparison claims to state-of-the-art delayed RL methods, explicitly includes goal-conditioned generalization, and calls joint belief-policy optimization essential. These extend the original headline claims without changing the central research objective.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations connecting Belief-IQL failures to exponentiated advantage errors, discusses prediction-accuracy versus computation tradeoffs, and interprets joint training as adapting beliefs to value-function errors. It also acknowledges that difficult AntMaze tasks may require goal-conditioned modifications and discusses transformer capacity and extreme-delay degradation. The earlier known-delay and vision-scaling limitations largely persist.

D1.justification: V2 adds a specific code repository URL, NVIDIA A5000/AMD EPYC hardware details, task-specific training-time examples, and ensemble/diffusion hyperparameter tables. The original transformer settings are retained, while the three-step setting disappears. Reproducibility documentation expands substantially, although the ensemble table repeats transformer settings and joint-training updates remain incompletely specified.

R1.justification: V2 adds a focused connection to classical delay compensation and Smith predictors, alongside references supporting differential-equation modeling, simulation, COMBO and dexterous manipulation. The three multi-step-return references disappear. The central positioning relative to offline RL and augmentation- versus belief-based delayed RL remains intact.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper, updates the byline, rewrites substantial introduction and related-work passages, moves related work from Section 6 to Section 2, and combines preliminaries with problem formulation. Experiments are reorganized from deterministic/stochastic subsections into task, baseline and ablation sections. Ethics, reproducibility and LLM-usage statements are added.

P2.justification: The original locomotion tables are relocated and expanded as compact Appendix Tables 7–8, while new main-text tables organize AntMaze and belief-baseline comparisons. V2 adds prediction-error, manipulation and long-delay plots, four rollout-image panels, and multiple ablation and implementation tables. Figure 1 and the document template/layout are also revised.

improvement.justification: V1 supported its method mainly with locomotion return tables, without controlled component ablations or seed-level uncertainty. V2 substantially strengthens that evidence through architecture, joint-training and data-availability tests, broader task and delay evaluations, three-seed variability, and additional reproducibility information. These additions help assess design choices and expose applicability limits while preserving the original results. Overstated AntMaze comparisons and incomplete joint-training/ensemble specifications limit the gains, but the added diagnostic evidence establishes a substantial net improvement.
